cushionCut.intro: Enter the ordered size of each cushion. The cuts update as you type.
cushionCut.ruleTitle: How the finished cover is sized
cushionCut.rule: The cover is made 1/4" smaller than the ordered width and depth, and the height is reduced by the deduction you pick (1/2" unless the job says otherwise). Foam is cut to the ordered size.
cushionCut.name: Cushion name
cushionCut.wrapHelp: Zipper runs the back and 4" up each side
cushionCut.backHelp: Zipper along the back edge only
cushionCut.frontHelp: The side the zipper runs along
cushionCut.fillIn: Fill in the three sizes to see the cuts.
cushionCut.clearConfirm: Clear every cushion and start over?
cushionCut.nameHelp: Optional. Shows on the cut list and printout.
cushionCut.directionHelp: Pick one if it matters. Decided by the project manager with the client.
cushionCut.fabricHelp: Optional. Enter it on each cushion if they use different fabrics.
cushionCut.jobHelp: These print at the top of the work order PDF.
cushionCut.stripsHelp: Strips are {{len}}" long, cut on the bias from 54" fabric, counted separately for each fabric.
cushionCut.foamNotesPlaceholder: e.g. HD36, layered: 1" soft over 4" firm
cushionCut.foamNotesHelp: For the project manager: foam type, and if it's layered. Foam is cut to the ordered size.
cushionCut.heightDeductionHelp: Usually 1/2". Pick more or less only when the job calls for it.
cushionCut.cordingHelp: Untick if this cushion has no cording.
cushionCut.shape_boxHelp: Box cushion with plates and boxing.
cushionCut.shape_wedgeHelp: Back wedge: deep at the bottom, thin at the top, sloped back rest.
cushionCut.lengthDeductionHelp: Usually 1/2". Only the length is made shorter.
cushionCut.wedgeZipperHelp: Full length, centered on the bottom.
cushionCut.shape_boardHelp: Upholstered to plywood: one plate on top, one boxing strip that wraps under the board, no zipper.
cushionCut.boardZipperHelp: Board-mounted: stapled to the plywood, no zipper.
cushionCut.boardBoxing: Boxing, all the way around (L × W)
cushionCut.fabricHelpLayout: Every cushion in the same fabric (and direction) is laid out together on a 54" roll, with one spare plate and the bias cording block, the same as the Fabric Yardage tool.

leafBag.intro: Enter each job's finished bag size. The cuts update as you type.
leafBag.rule: Cuts come from the bag size. Both pieces are bag width + 1". Long bottom is bag depth + 9" and short top is bag depth + 2 1/2". Leaf size is for reference only.
leafBag.pasteHelp: Copy the rows (Job #, Leaf Width, Leaf Depth, Bag Width, Bag Depth, Qty) from the spreadsheet, paste them here, then press Add rows.
leafBag.jobHelp: Prints on the cut list and labels.
leafBag.fillIn: Fill in the bag width and depth to see the cuts.
leafBag.clearConfirm: Clear every bag and start over?

cushionPricing.intro: Enter each cushion's size. Prices for every labor and insert option show as you type. Prices are per piece.
cushionPricing.addOns: Throw pillow labor {{pillow}} each · Welting +{{welt}} per piece · Outdoor Celeste Bio tick +{{tick}} per piece · COM: labor × 1.15. Tick add-ons on each section to include them in the quote.
cushionPricing.pasteHelp: Copy the rows (Name, Qty, Length, Depth, Thickness, and for a matching back: Back height, Back thickness, Seat fabric, Back fabric), paste them here, then press Add rows. Columns can be tab-separated or separated by |.
cushionPricing.name: Name
cushionPricing.fillIn: Fill in the length, depth/height and thickness to see prices.
cushionPricing.quoteHelp: Each cushion's labor, insert and add-ons are picked above. Total is price each × how many.
cushionPricing.clearConfirm: Clear every cushion and start over?
cushionPricing.withBack: Matching Back Cushion (Same Length, Same Line On The Quote)
cushionPricing.plywoodNote: Plywood is counted for the whole job: all plywood cushions are nested onto 4 × 8 sheets at {{price}} a sheet (see Plywood below the cushions).
cushionPricing.plywoodSummary: {{sheets}} sheets of 4 × 8 plywood for {{pieces}} pieces, at {{price}} a sheet = {{cost}}. Allows 1/8" saw kerf and 1/4" trim on each edge.
cushionPricing.plywoodTooBig: Bigger than a 4 × 8 sheet, so not counted. Confirm the seat breaks with the client, then enter each section as its own cushion:
cushionPricing.plywoodCardTooBig: Too long for one 4 × 8 sheet. Confirm seat breaks with the client and enter each section as its own cushion.
cushionPricing.copied: Copied. Paste it into Estimate Rocket.
cushionPricing.copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select the text and copy it instead.
cushionPricing.yardsEach: {{n}} yd each (exact {{exact}}), rounded up to whole yards
cushionPricing.addOnsHelp: Ticked add-ons are added to this cushion's price.
cushionPricing.addTick: Outdoor Celeste Bio Tick (+{{price}} Per Piece)
cushionPricing.fabricEachMany: Yards each are listed per section above
cushionPricing.yardageHow: Fabric is worked out by laying every cut piece on a 54" roll (with one spare plate and the bias cording for welted styles), the same as the Fabric Yardage tool. Add a pattern repeat for patterned fabric.
cushionPricing.fabricMapsHelp: Cushions in the same fabric are laid out together on one roll: {{order}} yd to order in all. The estimate lines above price each cushion on its own ({{separate}} yd).
cushionPricing.joinAbove: Add To The Estimate Rocket Line Above
cushionPricing.joinHelp: Tick this when this cushion has the same style, fill and fabric as the one above, so they share one line with every size listed.
cushionPricing.joinedNote: Same style, fill and fabric as {{name}}. Change them on that card.
cushionPricing.velcroHelp: Runs the length of each cushion, rounded to the nearest foot.
cushionPricing.designerHelp: Shown on every Estimate Rocket line: "According To (Designer) Design Specifications". Leave blank for "According To Design Specifications".

fabricYardage.intro: Add the cushions, or bring them in from Cushion Cut Dimensions. Every piece is laid out on the roll and the yardage updates as you type.
fabricYardage.v1: Pattern repeat is not handled yet. It follows the cutter's rulebook: every piece of a fabric runs the same way (railroaded when it fits; one-way fabrics up the roll), {{trim}} is trimmed off each selvage, pieces share cut lines, {{end}} is squared off the first end, bias cording comes from one block at the end ({{strip}} strips), there is enough left for one spare plate, and the order is rounded up to whole yards.
fabricYardage.import: Bring in from Cushion Cut Dimensions
fabricYardage.importConfirm: Replace these cushions with the ones in Cushion Cut Dimensions?
fabricYardage.importNone: Cushion Cut Dimensions has no finished cushions on this device yet.
fabricYardage.name: Cushion name
fabricYardage.fabricHelp: Cushions with the same fabric share one roll.
fabricYardage.eitherHelp: Plain fabric: each piece can turn whichever way saves fabric.
fabricYardage.upTheRollHelp: Every piece's width runs across the roll.
fabricYardage.railroadedHelp: Every piece is turned so its width runs along the roll.
fabricYardage.fillIn: Fill in the sizes to add this cushion's pieces.
fabricYardage.gapHelp: 0 means pieces share a cut line. If you need a gap, use at least 1/2".
fabricYardage.used: {{pct}}% of the roll used by pieces
fabricYardage.tooWide: {{piece}} ({{size}}) is wider than {{width}} the way it has to run. Railroad it, add a seam, or check the roll width. It is not counted in the yardage.
fabricYardage.diagram: Roll layout, first end on the left
fabricYardage.empty: Add a cushion to see the layout.
fabricYardage.extraHelp: Added on top of the layout before rounding up.
fabricYardage.togetherHelp: Each cushion's pieces stay together. Can take more fabric.
fabricYardage.mixedHelp: Off: like the cutters, the same pieces are cut together in chunks, largest first.
fabricYardage.selvageTrimHelp: Selvage plus room for the cutter's straight ruler line.
fabricYardage.dir_auto: Let the tool pick (railroad if possible)
fabricYardage.autoPicked: The tool picked {{way}}. Use the work order if it says otherwise.
fabricYardage.extraPlateHelp: Lays out a copy of the biggest plate so there is enough for one more.
fabricYardage.joinedTitle: Joined pieces: check the seams before cutting
fabricYardage.joinedRule: These are wider than the roll, so each is cut as a center and two mirrored ends, with 1/2" seam allowance at each join. Seams stay symmetrical and never on the front; front corners or mid-side need approval. Joined plates should be agreed with the client first.
fabricYardage.oneWayHelp: Velvet, mohair, chenille and directional prints. Every piece is cut up the roll, pointing the same way.
fabricYardage.autoPickedNap: One-way fabric: cut up the roll so the nap runs the same way on every piece.
fabricYardage.napRailroadTitle: Railroading a one-way fabric needs approval
fabricYardage.napRailroad: The nap will run side to side on the cushions. Check with Eva or the client before cutting.
fabricYardage.napLegend: Red arrows point down the nap. Find which way the nap runs on the roll and lay every piece with its arrow that way: plates run back edge to front edge, and boxing and zipper strips run top edge to bottom edge.
fabricYardage.patternRepeatHelp: From the fabric's spec. Leave at 0 for a plain fabric.
fabricYardage.patternHorizontalHelp: Blank = same as up and down.
fabricYardage.autoPickedPattern: Patterned: cut up the roll. Railroad only if the designer or work order approves.
fabricYardage.patternEstimate: Every plate, boxing and wedge piece sits with a motif centered on it; zippers go anywhere. Where the motifs fall across the roll is luck, so this is the worst of four starting points. Have a cutter lay it out before cutting.
fabricYardage.offCenter_one: {{count}} piece can't land centered on a motif across the roll and is placed off center. Check with the designer.
fabricYardage.offCenter_other: {{count}} pieces can't land centered on a motif across the roll and are placed off center. Check with the designer.
fabricYardage.heldAtPlain: This pattern packs tighter than the plain-fabric layout, so the estimate is held at the plain yardage.
fabricYardage.motifLegend: Dots mark the motif each piece is centered on.
fabricYardage.boardHelp: Board-mounted: finished sizes, one plate and one boxing strip that wraps under the board, no zipper.

upholstery.intro: Follows "How to price upholstery labor": base labor, cushions, foam, yardage, supplies, then upcharges. The estimate at the bottom copies straight into Estimate Rocket.
upholstery.newConfirm: Clear this estimate and start a new one?
upholstery.oversizeNone: No oversize charge for this type
upholstery.noSlip: No slipcover price is listed for this type, so upholstery labor is used.
upholstery.noCushions: No cushions included in base labor. Add each if the piece has loose cushions.
upholstery.yardsHint: Piece {{piece}} yd + cushions {{cushions}} yd = {{total}} yd charged (whole yards). The chart yardage doesn't include cushions; their fabric is always added. Leave blank to use the chart.
upholstery.fabricPriceHelp: Leave blank if the client supplies the fabric
upholstery.suppliesNote: Upholstery supplies use the same quantity as the yardage.
upholstery.tufting: Tufting (biscuit or diamond): add {{pct}}% to base labor
upholstery.trimNeedWD: Enter the width and depth in step 1 to price trim.
upholstery.trimNeedWDH: Enter the width, depth and height in step 1 to price trim.
upholstery.white: White fabric: add {{pct}}% to total labor
upholstery.ratesHelp: Cushion and foam rates match the Cushion Pricing calculator. Saved on this device.
upholstery.copied: Copied. Paste it into Estimate Rocket.
upholstery.quotedHelp: Prints as "QUOTED SOLID/RAILROADED" on the estimate.
upholstery.armHelp: Adds "Additional Charge if Changing Style" when changed.

hist.title: History check
hist.none: No past Estimate Rocket prices for this type yet.
hist.inLine: This estimate's labor ({{labor}}) is in line with past jobs.
hist.higher: This estimate's labor ({{labor}}) is {{pct}}% above what similar past pieces were priced at. Worth a second look.
hist.lower: This estimate's labor ({{labor}}) is {{pct}}% below what similar past pieces were priced at. Worth a second look.
hist.laborOnly: Compares labor only, because past estimates priced fabric and foam separately.
hist.slipFallback: Too few past slipcovers, so reupholstery prices are shown.

draperyPleat.intro: Figure one panel at a time. Pick the draw so the diagram shows which side the lead edge and return go on.
draperyPleat.name: Panel / location
draperyPleat.finishedHelp: After pleating. Half the rod width for pairs.
draperyPleat.legend: Blue = lead edge and return · Yellow = pleat · Green = space · Dots = pins
draperyPleat.adds: The layout adds up to {{total}} (hemmed width {{hemmed}}). Pleat and space widths round to the nearest 1/8".
draperyPleat.tooNarrow: The hemmed width isn't wider than the finished width plus the return and lead edge, so there's nothing left for pleats.
draperyPleat.fillIn: Fill in the hemmed and finished widths to see the layout.
draperyPleat.clearConfirm: Clear this panel and start over?
draperyPleat.draw_leftHelp: Stacks on the left. Return on the left, lead edge on the right (as seen from the room).
draperyPleat.draw_rightHelp: Stacks on the right. Lead edge on the left, return on the right (as seen from the room).
draperyPleat.draw_bothHelp: A pair: make 2 panels, mirror images. Lead edges meet in the middle. Enter half the rod width as the finished width.
